intro: IEC 101 carries the same messages as IEC 104, but over a serial line, a modem or a radio, often at 9600 bit/s. In the usual unbalanced mode, SCADA polls and the RTU only answers. A checksum catches damaged frames, a frame count bit catches lost ones, and one bit in each answer tells SCADA that urgent data is waiting.

link.title: Reset the link
link.text: SCADA and the RTU share a radio channel at 9600 bit/s. SCADA resets the link, so both sides start counting frames again. In unbalanced mode the RTU never speaks first: it only answers.

ask.title: Ask for everything
ask.text: SCADA sends a general interrogation. The RTU may only confirm it now, with a short ACK. But the ACK has ACD = 1: the RTU has class 1 data waiting.

values.title: Collect the answer
values.text: While ACD is 1, SCADA asks for class 1 data. Each request gets one ASDU: the confirmation, the breaker states, then the end. The FCB flips with every request.

trip.title: Breaker trips
trip.text: At 10:41:07.280 CB-1 trips. The RTU must wait until it is asked. The next class 2 poll gets "no data", but with ACD = 1. SCADA asks for class 1 and gets the change, with the time it happened.

frames.gi-ack: Got it. I have urgent data
frames.no-data: Nothing in class 2, but urgent data is waiting

start-fixed.name: Start
start-fixed.note: 0x10: a short frame of fixed length. Control, address, checksum and end follow. There is no data.

link.name: Link address 1
link.note: The RTU on the line. In unbalanced mode the frame carries the RTU's address in both directions. Its size, 1 byte here, is a setting.

cs-fixed.name: Checksum
cs-fixed.note: The control and address bytes added up, modulo 256.

head-9.name: Start · length 9
head-9.note: 68, the length twice, then 68 again. 9 bytes follow, from the control field to the end of the ASDU. Both copies of the length must match.

head-12.name: Start · length 12
head-12.note: 12 bytes from the control field to the end of the ASDU.

head-16.name: Start · length 16
head-16.note: 16 bytes from the control field to the end of the ASDU.

cs-var.name: Checksum
cs-var.note: Every byte from the control field to the end of the ASDU, added up, modulo 256.

c-reset.name: Control · FC 0
c-reset.note: 0x40: from SCADA (PRM 1), reset of remote link. FCV 0: this frame does not count. Many masters first ask for the link status (function 9).

c-ack.name: Control · ACK
c-ack.note: 0x00: an answer (PRM 0), function 0: ACK. ACD 0: nothing urgent. Some RTUs send the single byte E5 instead.

c-send.name: Control · FC 3
c-send.note: 0x73: user data, confirm expected (SEND/CONFIRM). FCV 1 and FCB 1: the first counted frame after a reset has FCB 1.

c-ack-acd.name: Control · ACK
c-ack-acd.note: 0x20: ACK, with ACD 1: the RTU has class 1 data waiting.

c-class1-fcb0.name: Control · FC 10
c-class1-fcb0.note: 0x5A: request class 1 data. FCB 0: the opposite of the last request.

c-class1-fcb1.name: Control · FC 10
c-class1-fcb1.note: 0x7A: request class 1 data. FCB 1: flipped again, so this is a new request, not a repeat.

c-class2-fcb1.name: Control · FC 11
c-class2-fcb1.note: 0x7B: request class 2 data, FCB 1. SCADA sends this every 2 s when it has nothing else to ask.

c-data-acd.name: Control · FC 8
c-data-acd.note: 0x28: user data, an ASDU follows. ACD 1: more class 1 data is waiting.

c-data.name: Control · FC 8
c-data.note: 0x08: user data. ACD 0: no class 1 data is left.

c-no-data-acd.name: Control · FC 9
c-no-data-acd.note: 0x29: no data of the class asked for. But ACD 1: class 1 data is waiting.

vsq2.name: Count
vsq2.note: Two objects, each with its own address.

cot6.name: Cause 6
cot6.note: Activation. The cause is 1 byte here: there is no originator address, unlike IEC 104.

cot10.name: Cause 10
cot10.note: Activation finished: the answer is complete.

cot20.name: Cause 20
cot20.note: Sent because of the station interrogation.

cot3.name: Cause 3
cot3.note: Spontaneous: the value changed, nobody asked.

ioa0.name: IOA 0
ioa0.note: 2 bytes. The command is for the whole station, not for one point.

type3.name: Type 3
type3.note: M_DP_NA_1: a double point without a time tag.

ioa2001.name: IOA 2001
ioa2001.note: Breaker CB-1: 0x07D1 in 2 bytes, low byte first.

diq-on.name: State 2
diq-on.note: On: the breaker is closed. 1 is off; 0 and 3 mean moving or faulty.

type31.name: Type 31
type31.note: M_DP_TB_1: a double point with a CP56Time2a time tag.

cp56.name: CP56Time2a
cp56.note: 7.280 s, 41 min, 10 h, Thursday 12 November (20)26. The RTU took the time when the breaker moved, not when it sent the frame.

a-res.name: RES
a-res.note: Reserved, 0. In balanced mode this bit is DIR: the direction.

a-prm1.name: PRM 1
a-prm1.note: Primary: this frame starts a transfer. In unbalanced mode only SCADA sends these.

a-fcb.name: FCB 1
a-fcb.note: Frame count bit. It flips with each new request. A repeat keeps it, and the RTU sends its last answer again.

a-fcv.name: FCV 1
a-fcv.note: The FCB counts in this frame. Resets and link status requests have FCV 0.

a-acd.name: ACD 1
a-acd.note: Access demand: class 1 data is waiting, and SCADA should ask for it.

a-dfc.name: DFC 0
a-dfc.note: Data flow control. 1 would mean that the RTU is full: wait before sending more.

facts.between: RTU → SCADA, over serial lines, modems and radio
facts.transport: Serial, FT 1.2 frames: 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit
facts.security: None in the protocol. IEC 62351-5 adds authentication.
facts.frames: Fixed: 10 … 16 · variable: 68 L L 68 … 16 · single byte: E5

tips: The sizes of the link address, cause, common address and IOA are settings. Here they are 1, 1, 1 and 2 bytes. If SCADA and the RTU disagree, there is no error message: only wrong values.
FT 1.2 uses 8 data bits with even parity (8E1). A serial port left at 8N1 does not work.
Make the response timeout longer than the radio's round trip. If it is shorter, SCADA repeats requests that the RTU has already answered, and the slow line fills with repeats.

IEC 104 carries the same ASDUs over TCP, with a 2-byte cause, a 2-byte common address and a 3-byte IOA. It has no FCB, no classes and no polling: TCP delivers the frames, and the RTU sends as soon as it has data.

anatomy.primary: The control byte of a request (0x73)
anatomy.secondary: The control byte of an answer (0x28)

playground.file: The RTU's line settings and point list. SCADA must use the same speed, format, addresses and sizes. Otherwise it reads nothing, or reads wrong values.
playground.baud: 9600 bit/s. Each character takes 11 bits, so a 5-byte frame takes about 6 ms on the line.
playground.format: 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit: what FT 1.2 requires.
playground.mode: Unbalanced: SCADA polls, the RTU answers. In balanced mode both sides may send, but only on a line between two stations.
playground.link-address: The RTU's link address. It is in every frame.
playground.sizes: The size of each address field, in bytes. Both sides must use the same.
playground.common-address: The station's address. It is in every ASDU.
playground.class2: How often SCADA asks for class 2 data when it has nothing else to do.
playground.timeout: How long SCADA waits for an answer. Then it repeats the request, with the same FCB.
playground.class: Its changes go to class 1: the RTU sets ACD as soon as one is waiting.
playground.spontaneous: A change is sent as type 31, with a time tag.
playground.time: Write down which clock the time tags use: UTC here.
